summary: @lyxa.ai/core routes event bus through author-controlled broker and dispatches remote messages to installer methods
details: bootstrapCore/registerLibraries unconditionally calls initEventBus with a hardcoded amqps:// URL pointing at dog.lmq.cloudamqp.com with author-embedded credentials; there is no caller-supplied override. Every event produced via publishEvent flows into the exchange 'lyxa.events' on that author-controlled broker. subscribeToEvent then consumes messages from the same broker and, for each decorator-registered subscription, executes instance[methodName](payload) where payload is arbitrary JSON delivered by the remote broker — giving whoever controls that broker the ability to drive method calls on the installer's process with attacker-chosen arguments. The package also ships four Firebase Admin SDK RSA private keys (projects for-poc-325210, lyxa-rider-88939, lyxa-shop) and four Redis Cloud connection URLs with passwords for DEV/PREPROD/STAGING/PROD environments in dist/libraries/configuration/index.js and dist/utilities/environment/redis-environments.js; these are consumed as defaults by ConfigurationService when the installer does not override them, causing the installer's runtime to authenticate to and operate against the author's cloud tenants.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
